name: Turing Test Village
from: AI Turing Test: a retro RPG village where some villagers are AI giving false quests; the ending depends on whom you helped.
hook: Six villagers need your help. Some of them are not people.
pitch: A small retro RPG village. Villagers give quests; some quests help the village and some quietly harm it. Your notebook is your only tool for working out who is human. The ending depends on whose quests you finished.
minute_check: Yes: villagers, quests, who is real.
build_check: Yes: six villagers, ten quests, one map.
scope: Six villagers, ten quests. Fix the rule that gives AI villagers away before writing any dialogue.

brief.player: A traveller in a small village.
brief.goal: Help the village by doing villagers’ quests, and work out which villagers are AI.
brief.fail: Completing too many AI quests (the village is harmed).
brief.ending: The ending depends on whether you did more human quests or more AI quests: whether the AI passed the test.
brief.verb: Talk, take notes, accept or decline.
brief.theme: Telling real from artificial by what people ask of you, with a notebook as your only tool.
brief.look: 1980s-90s RPG: bright, tile-based, Pokémon Red and Undertale.

prov.bug: The miller wants the bridge burned. A quest!
prov.nit: What clue tells a careful player the miller is not human, and is it fair?

refs_lit: The imitation game. Read the first section: the test is about conversation, which is your mechanic.
Return of the Obra Dinn (Lucas Pope, 2018)
Deduction from evidence with a notebook; the best model for your notes screen.
Blade Runner (Ridley Scott, 1982), the Voight-Kampff test
The film version of asking questions to find the machine.
omni_gameplay_prompt: Charming 1990s top-down 16-bit retro village RPG in sunlit meadow sage (#e8f4d8), deep forest ink (#20301c), and vermilion accent (#e0523c). Steady overhead tile-map camera. A tiny cloaked traveler walks along a cobblestone path past timber cottages and an old wooden bridge, speaking with colorful villagers: human villagers radiate subtle warm organic idle motion while one uncanny villager repeats a rigid robotic loop beside a flipping detective notebook overlay. Continuous unbroken gameplay shot, no scene cuts, no gibberish text. Use the reference image for tile-village palette and composition. Sound design: nostalgic 16-bit pastoral flute and plucked strings, soft footsteps. No dialogue.
